issues.issue: "servicing agent and/or the owner and holder" leaves it indeterminate in what capacity Aurora contracts and whether it holds the Note at all. The "and/or" formulation permits either reading of the party's identity and authority.

"a mortgage, deed of trust or comparable security instrument" identifies the Security Instrument only by an open alternative including the vague word "comparable". Which document is the "Security Instrument" is therefore established by inference rather than identification.

The definition as written is a fragment — the subject ("The Note and") is missing — so grammatically only the Security Instrument is collectively defined as the "Loan Documents". Since "Loan Documents" drives sections 3, 6, 13 and 21, the omission changes the scope of those provisions.

The recital fixes the Arrearage at $13,755.30 as the sum to be repaid, while Attachment A § b states the plan payments will not cure it; whether the Agreement disposes of the stated Arrearage is left open. The itemised figures do reconcile arithmetically, so the tension is with Attachment A rather than internal.

"Corporate Advances" is defined by an open catch-all ("include, but are not limited to") over a list of specific servicing fees, so what other charges may be loaded into the Arrearage is unbounded. Whether ejusdem generis confines the category to the enumerated foreclosure/preservation-type fees is exactly what a borrower would contest.

"Other Fees" is defined non-exhaustively ("include, but are not limited to") with only two examples, giving the general category no ascertainable boundary. The two specifics are too thin to limit the catch-all by ejusdem generis.

This recital asserts as fact that Lender "has so accelerated and declared due in full" and "may have already commenced foreclosure proceedings", while the immediately following recital states no foreclosure has been commenced and paragraph 8 treats acceleration only conditionally ("if the Lender previously notified the Customer"). The recitals and operative paragraph 8 thus point in different directions on whether the loan is in fact accelerated.

This recital states no foreclosure proceeding has been commenced and no sale scheduled, yet paragraph 4 addresses postponement of "a foreclosure sale" and Lender's freedom not to dismiss "a pending foreclosure proceeding", and paragraph 8 speaks of foreclosure resuming "from the point at which it was placed on hold". The recital and those operative paragraphs cannot both describe the same state of affairs.

The recital assumes "any foreclosure action that may now be pending", directly at odds with the preceding recital that Lender "has not commenced Foreclosure proceedings" and that no sale has been scheduled. The two consecutive recitals give inconsistent accounts of the foreclosure posture the forbearance operates on.

The recital says Lender agreed "to allow Customer to repay the Arrearage" under the workout, but Attachment A § b states the aggregate plan payments will be insufficient to pay the Arrearage and the account will remain delinquent. A borrower reading the recital as a promise of a cure meets an operative term that promises the opposite.

"will not have personal liability on the debt pursuant to this Agreement" can mean either that no personal liability arises on the underlying debt or only that this Agreement creates none. The qualifier "pursuant to this Agreement" attaches ambiguously to "liability" or to "debt".

"forbear from exercising any or all of its rights and remedies" is ambiguous as to whether Lender must forbear from all remedies or may choose which ones to forbear from. The disjunctive "any or all" makes the extent of the only promise Lender gives indeterminate.

The forbearance promise sits against paragraph 4 (no obligation to dismiss a pending foreclosure) and paragraph 7 (nothing herein waives the right to commence or resume foreclosure), which together may leave the forbearance with nothing to operate on. Whether Lender actually gave up anything during the term turns on reconciling section 3 with those clauses.

The paragraph presupposes a foreclosure sale and "a pending foreclosure proceeding", which contradicts the recital stating Lender has not commenced foreclosure proceedings and no sale has been scheduled. It also qualifies section 3's forbearance by relieving Lender of any duty to dismiss.

"or otherwise fails to comply with any of the terms and conditions herein or therein" is a catch-all sitting on a specific payment-default trigger, so any trivial non-compliance may count as a "Default" permitting immediate foreclosure. The parenthetical also miswrites "any such even" for "event", leaving the defined term's antecedent imprecise.

"a waiver of any of all of the Lender's rights" is a miswriting of "any or all", leaving the scope of what is preserved grammatically unresolved. The error goes to the reach of the non-waiver, which is the whole point of the clause.

Preserving "the right to commence or resume foreclosure proceedings" during the Agreement is difficult to square with section 3, under which Lender "shall forbear" from exercising its rights and remedies while there is no Default. Read literally, section 7 would let Lender foreclose despite a performing Customer.

"will not be withdrawn unless Lender determines to do so by applicable law" is garbled and can be read either as Lender's unilateral discretion or as a legal requirement. The sentence's condition on withdrawal of a foreclosure cannot be applied as written.

The paragraph assumes a commenced foreclosure that was "placed on hold", contradicting the recital that Lender has not commenced foreclosure proceedings and no sale is scheduled. It also preserves collection action in terms that qualify the section 3 forbearance.

The heading "Limited Modification" suggests the Agreement modifies the Loan Documents, while the text ratifies them in full and Attachment A a.2 says tender of the Sixth Plan payment is not acceptance of a loan modification. Whether this Agreement modified the Note at all is left unresolved across those provisions.

"shall be applied, at Lender's sole option, first to the earliest monthly payment under the Note that is due" combines a mandatory application rule with unfettered discretion, and "less than the full payment under then due and owing" is missing a word. It cannot be told whether Lender must apply payments in the stated order or may do as it chooses.

The clause is numbered 11 but refers to "the requirements of this paragraph 10", a cross-reference error that points at the Application of Payments section instead. Which paragraph's requirements make a payment non-conforming is therefore uncertain.

"reported monthly to all credit reporting agencies for the duration of this Agreement and thereafter" leaves "thereafter" without any end point or condition. The provision does not say for how long, or on what basis, the pre-existing delinquent status continues to be reported.

"all other amounts Customer agreed to pay" and "other amounts that may attain priority over the Security Instrument" are open catch-alls whose breach is made a Default, without boundary against the enumerated taxes and insurance premiums. A borrower could not know which unpaid charges trigger foreclosure.

The integration clause says the Agreement supersedes all prior understandings, yet the accompanying cover letter states "Not withstanding anything to the contrary contained in the Special Forbearance Agreement" and that signing "in no way affects or eliminates any rights you have been given in this letter". Whether the letter's terms survive section 14 is a live conflict.

Strict time-of-the-essence for the Attachment A Due Dates sits awkwardly with paragraph 11 and paragraph 7's footnote, which let Lender accept non-conforming or untimely payments in its sole discretion, and with Attachment A a.1's First Plan payment date of 11/18/2009 against the 11/15/2009 Agreement Return Date. Which date the Customer must actually meet turns on reconciling these.

The proviso that no severance is effective "if it materially changes the economic benefit of this Agreement to either party" uses an undefined materiality standard that could defeat the whole severability mechanism. What counts as a material change to economic benefit has no benchmark in the Agreement.

The First Plan payment is due "on or before 11/18/2009", but the same Attachment A makes the Agreement "of no force and effect" unless Lender receives the executed Agreement and the First Plan payment by the 11/15/2009 Agreement Return Date, and the cover letter also demands the payment by 11/15/2009. The two deadlines for the same payment cannot both stand.

The paragraph imposes on the Customer a duty to supply information "to enable Lender to properly evaluate" a "request for a loan modification or other workout option" without stating any corresponding obligation on Lender, and "other workout option" is undefined. Whether Lender thereby promised to evaluate or offer anything is exactly what the words leave open.

The disclaimer that "Tender of the Sixth Plan payment shall not be deemed acceptance ... of a workout plan or loan modification" is hard to reconcile with the recital that Lender agreed to let Customer repay the Arrearage "pursuant to a loan work-out arrangement" and with Attachment A § b's requirement to enter a "Cure Method". The Agreement both anticipates and disclaims a workout outcome.

This paragraph states the plan payments will not cure the Arrearage and the account will remain delinquent, which contradicts the recital that Lender agreed to allow Customer "to repay the Arrearage pursuant to a loan work-out arrangement" and sits against section 3's forbearance and section 4's reinstatement language. What the Customer obtains by full performance is left genuinely inconsistent.
